## agents

- **Telling agents 'never run the whole suite' also makes them skip the selected ci gate unless the brief names the allowed gate.** Telling agents 'never run the whole suite' also makes them skip the selected ci gate unless the brief names the allowed gate. Five items merged with ci and bug_hunt recorded unavailable because the brief said no whole-suite runs; `ddflow tests` also prints the full-suite command, which two other agents then ran (13k tests, 20+ minutes). Say both halves: the selected-scope `gate run ITEM ci` is required before merge; only a manual whole-suite pytest is forbidden. Brief text now carries this. `[L-forbid-wording-skips-allowed-gate]`
- **A background wait loop must end by itself: a deadline, a liveness check, and stopped before the agent reports.** Background wait loops need a deadline and a liveness check (not just a clean-exit marker), must never pgrep -f a string in their own command, and must be stopped before the agent reports; otherwise they poll for hours after the work is gone. `[L-wait-loops-end]`

- **A hand-built TOML writer must parse its own output before replacing the file.** json.dumps is valid TOML only for strings, numbers and arrays of them; a dict becomes JSON, which TOML rejects. Any writer that assembles TOML by string formatting must render tables as TOML inline tables and parse the merged result (tomllib.loads) before the atomic write, so a malformed block is refused instead of leaving a config no later command can load. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-B-reviewers-add-launch-json]`
- **A set-valued lookup must union every match, not stop at the first.** When a substring map returns a SET that a safety check compares against, take the union of every matching key (and treat any empty match as unknown); first-match-wins on key order under-approximates the set and turns into a false pass. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-B15af2d6420]`
- **Never let 0 (or "") mean both 'unset' and a real value: use None for unset.** When a numeric or string option has a default, represent 'not given' as None on every surface (argparse default=None, MCP a.get(k) is None) and validate the explicit value; `x or DEFAULT` silently turns an explicit 0/'' into the default, and in a safety tool that flips the answer in the unsafe direction. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-B22-minzero]`
- **A hook counts as armed only if the thing that runs it would run ddflow's check on every commit.** When detecting another tool's hook (pre-commit framework), model its skip rules -- stages/default_stages, file filters without always_run, pass_filenames, language fail/pygrep, remote manifests -- and report anything unreadable or unverifiable as NOT installed with the reason; three reviewers each found a false 'installed' the first version missed. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-B259fd32dbd]`
- **A 'last line is the max' shortcut only holds while a file has exactly one writer; merge=union silently gives it two.** Any O(1) summary read from an append-only file's tail (clock, counter, high-water mark) is valid only under a single-writer invariant. - **A git hook's reads must not depend on which GIT_* variables the runner kept: run them in the committing tree.** Commit-hook git reads run in the tree being committed (the hook's cwd toplevel, if it belongs to this repository), inheriting GIT_INDEX_FILE; never git -C <primary>. ## ci

- **Python 3.12.3 argparse breaks '--' for pytest: never rely on it to protect a dash-led argument.** Do not use '--' to make a user-supplied value safe from an option parser: check it yourself and ./-prefix it. A test green on dev Python (3.12.13/3.13) can fail on the runner's 3.12.3. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-py3123-argparse-double-dash]`
- **A change to the default pipelines must run the slow scenarios before it lands.** When a default gate, pipeline or completion rule changes, run 'pytest tests/test_scenarios.py -m slow' before merging: the unit_tests gate runs addopts' 'not slow', so the scenarios that drive a phase to completion never see the change, and CI is the first place they run. _(first paragraph)_ `[L081419cc36]`
- **A worker count fixed in a committed hook (-n auto) is per-core on the host that runs it.** Substitute the computed count in the local runner (a temp copy of the hook config), keep the committed config for CI, and bound concurrent full runs host-wide _(first paragraph)_ `[L2e0370b0a4]`
- **A change to ddflow/api makes ddflow tests and the ci gate the whole suite (about 16 minutes).** Prefer putting new logic in a module no hub imports; budget a full ci run when ddflow.api changes; use gate run ci --rerun-failed after a fix _(first paragraph)_ `[L787983322f]`
- **A hook-line change merged with tests/test_compaction_summary.py still asserting the old line.** When a generated command line changes, grep tests for the old literal, not only the selector's reach _(first paragraph)_ `[Lf087875409]`

## flaky

- **A lapsed lease's revival is judged on the globs it held; the item's new globs belong to the heartbeat catch-up.** When checking a heartbeat revival for overlaps, use lease.globs only _(first paragraph)_ `[L-revival-judged-on-lease-globs]`

- **Back up files by their full path, never by basename, before swapping in an old version to prove a test fails.** When copying files aside to run tests against HEAD's version, key the backup by the repo-relative path (or use git show into a temp tree); several modules share a basename (api/rules.py, surfaces/commands/rules.py, surfaces/tools/rules.py) _(first paragraph)_ `[L1358db6e92]`
- **Delete a background run's output file before polling it; an old 'PASSED' in it ends the wait early.** Reusing /tmp/..._ut.out across runs makes 'until grep PASSED' return at once on the previous run's text; rm -f the file (or use a unique name) before launching _(first paragraph)_ `[L148a6b71a8]`
- **Run the suite without a PYTHONPATH pinned at the source tree: test_build_probe then probes the source, not the wheel, and fails.** For unit_tests, run uv run pytest from the worktree with PYTHONPATH unset (env -u PYTHONPATH); never pin PYTHONPATH=<tree> for the full suite _(first paragraph)_ `[L185edcda1d]`
- **A flaky brief test came from the cwd, not the load.** Before pinning config to fix a flake, diff the two outputs; session-start warns about the CALLER's worktree drift, so tests must run subprocesses with cwd=repo _(first paragraph)_ `[L32e7e00584]`
- **Never run uv run --active in a worktree: it repoints the shared primary venv's editable install at that worktree.** In a task worktree run plain `uv run`, or call the tool from the worktree's own .venv. The shell exports VIRTUAL_ENV as the primary's .venv, so `uv run --active` syncs THAT venv to the worktree's project and rewrites _editable_impl_ddflow_mcp.pth. Every lane's `ddflow` then runs that worktree's code, and when the worktree is removed `ddflow` stops importing on the whole host. _(first paragraph)_ `[L4424bd3d63]`
- **A confirmed triage's probe names the passing check, not the failure it fixed.** When triaging a finding --confirmed, write the probe as the test or command that now passes (and the fix commit), never as a description of the failing scenario. _(first paragraph)_ `[L4b6ce3681b]`
- **reviewed_head is recorded on every round, not only --commit reviews.** reviewed_head is generic round evidence (the head the diff was captured from), present on worktree and --commit rounds alike; a fallback that treats it as the reviewed tree must fire only when the round named no tree of its own, else a dirty-tree round is read as the clean commit and triage can pass work no reviewer saw. `[L4c24696616]`

- **Convention scans of declared modules must not import api-heavy CLI-only families.** A discovery scan over declared/*.py imports every match; gate the MCP tool table on tool= text and tolerate false text matches by checking the attribute _(first paragraph)_ `[La527bd3ef3]`

## git

- **Never git stash in a worktree: the stash stack is shared by every worktree and agent.** The git stash stack is shared across all worktrees. Parallel lanes that stash or pop destroy or steal each other's changes. Commit WIP instead. `[L-never-git-stash]`
- **git grep -o undercounts with many -F patterns: re-match whole lines instead.** To learn WHICH of many fixed-string patterns occur, run git grep without -o and re-match the returned lines in Python _(first paragraph)_ `[L5808fe73f8]`

## globs

- **ddflow's glob overlap check is conservative about *: a * in a directory position overlaps almost everything.** overlap() is conservative: a * in a directory position makes a task look like it overlaps everything, serialising parallel lanes. match() is not the problem. `[L-glob-overlap-is-conservative]`
- **A wildcard task glob makes the scheduler treat the task as overlapping every sibling under its prefix.** Broad globs overlap by prefix in the scheduler and block parallel lanes; use literal paths. `[L-wildcard-globs-scheduler-overlap]`

- **A refactor that deletes a deferred import must lower that module's guard baseline in the same change.** Run tests/test_architecture_guards.py when a change removes a function-level import or other counted pattern _(first paragraph)_ `[L22af420557]`

- **A branch cut before a config knob cannot commit until it merges main: merge with --no-commit first.** When a salvaged/stale worktree's commit hook dies with 'unknown knob' on the primary's .ddflow/config.toml, set the uncommitted work aside as a patch, run 'git merge main --no-commit', commit the merge, then re-apply and commit the work. _(first paragraph)_ `[L1907ee4695]`

## identity

- **Never keep your ddflow identity in a file another agent can rewrite: pass --agent on the command line itself.** Spell --agent <id> (or DDFLOW_AGENT) inline on every ddflow call; do not rely on a wrapper script in a scratch directory. _(first paragraph)_ `[La096a4fab1]`

## lanes

- **Never run a generically named script from a scratchpad lanes share: another lane's script runs under its identity.** The scratchpad is shared by every lane of the session, so a generic script name there can be replaced by another lane. Run commands inline or use lane-named files read back before each run. `[L57498f324b]`

## leases

- **A '**' glob conflicts with every live claim under its literal prefix: claim literal paths when a sibling holds a file in the same directory.** globs_overlap is prefix-based by design: 'templates/prompts/**/x.md' overlaps 'templates/prompts/y.md' although no file matches both. When a claim is refused for an overlap that cannot be real, narrow the claim's --globs to the literal paths (and widen later with ddflow update once the holder finishes) rather than waiting for or forcing past the holder. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-glob-prefix-overlap]`

## load

- **The load-per-core governor only acts in `parallel = auto`; a fixed cap bypasses it, and agent launches by hand bypass it too.** The load-per-core governor only acts in `parallel = auto`; a fixed cap bypasses it, and agent launches by hand bypass it too. Local config had parallel = fixed at 7 while two `pytest -n 48` full suites ran at once and load hit 119-160 on a 192-core host. Keep parallel = auto with load_per_core high = 0.80 and a raised max_parallel_max; take the offered count from `ddflow next` before launching agents; never run two full suites at once (DX-suite-host-lock). `[L-load-governor-needs-auto]`

## mcp

- **An api function behind an MCP tool's payload key must carry that key on every path, refusals included.** A tool that declares `payload: "<key>"` evaluates `out.body("<key>")` BEFORE it renders a refusal, so an api function that returns a bare `O.refused(...)` with no data raises `KeyError` over MCP and the client sees an opaque internal error -- while the CLI looks fine, because the CLI prints `out.reason` itself. Every outcome path, refusals included, must carry the projected key. `[L-mcp-payload-keys-on-every-path]`
- **A budget turned report-only must be relaxed in every enforcing site.** When a hard limit becomes report-only (D-mcp-budget-report), grep every enforcer: upgrade_dryrun.tools_problems and test_kind_data_surface still hard-failed the 100,000 cap _(first paragraph)_ `[L4749e7a4a0]`
- **A new top-level CLI command needs a covered-by declaration or tests/test_mcp_parity.py fails only in ci.** When adding a CLI verb that rides an existing MCP tool as an action, also add Command(path=(verb,), reason=...) in surfaces/declared _(first paragraph)_ `[Lf867ef729c]`

- **Derived files dirtied in the primary checkout block every agent's merge: keep the primary clean.** Derived files dirtied in the primary checkout block every agent's merge: keep the primary clean. pins regenerate, upgrade --apply and a hook left .gitattributes, .ddflow/.gitignore and README.md edited; four agents lost time and one used --allow-dirty. Before launching agents run `git -C PRIMARY status --short`; revert or commit derived files through a chore claim; never --allow-dirty. `[L-dirty-primary-blocks-merge]`
- **Check gate status before ddflow merge; chained commands skip the check.** Run ddflow gate status and read every box before merge; never chain gate run, record, merge and complete in one command _(first paragraph)_ `[L0e4a32a8c1]`

## mutation

- **Pick the tests for a mutation by file, not by covered line.** When judging a mutant, run every test file that reaches the module, not only the tests whose coverage context touches the mutated line, and run the sample against a real git checkout (a git archive copy fails 8 repo-shape tests, a full-suite -x run then 'kills' everything). _(first paragraph)_ `[L-mutation-sample-select-by-file-not-line]`
- **A gate that checks a committed ref cannot be proved by a working-tree mutation.** Before registering a mutation for a gate, check what the gate reads: gate verify edits the worktree uncommitted, so a gate that checks HEAD (ci) reports PASSED on mutated source and the proof is vacuous in the wrong direction. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-verify-mutates-the-worktree-ci-reads-head]`

## onboarding

- **Check an import's dropped and held items against the project's own handoff/status document before trusting the queue.** Verify import dispositions against the handoff doc `[L-import-read-against-handoff]`
- **ddflow setup and import land in the PRIMARY checkout even when run from a linked worktree: onboard a project on its default branch, not on a feature branch.** Onboarding writes to the primary checkout by design; do it there `[L-onboard-is-from-primary]`

## orchestrator

- **Long-pipeline lane subagents die silently right before their report; wave triage recovers all work from the item state.** In one Kilo/ddflow wave, 6 long-pipeline task subagents (claim + all gates + review rounds + suite runs through merge/complete in one agent) exited with EMPTY task results. All deaths happened at the final-stretch; every agent driving a SHORT tail (one gate set, one-line report) completed. Every death was triage-lossless: check item state + ddflow recover, salvage the worktree, send a one-line finisher. Prevention that held: small slices per subagent, narrow claim globs, end main agents at the last long gate and hand merge/complete to a finisher, one-word gate outputs. Mechanism: ddflow already flags the corpse (expired lease / interrupted + last gate states); the recovery verb is ddflow recover. See also lanes-watchdog task for the standard feature. `[Ld72d184d9a]`

## parallel-agents

- **Leases claimed for subagents expire during long work: the coordinator keeps them alive.** When a coordinator claims items for subagents (ddflow --agent <name> claim), nobody heartbeats unless told to: a subagent's run plus its review round easily exceeds lease.ttl_s (30 min), the lease lapses, and ddflow next offers the item again while its author is still editing the worktree. Either instruct each subagent to heartbeat, or run one background loop that heartbeats every delegated lease … _(first paragraph)_ `[L-delegated-leases-heartbeat]`

## pins

- **A hook's all-paths-are-mine guard fails whenever ddflow's own event shards are dirty.** Never gate a derived-file commit on the whole working tree being clean: ddflow keeps uncommitted event shards in the primary; gate on what would be STAGED _(first paragraph)_ `[L7b29928371]`

## priority

- **In ddflow a LOWER priority number runs sooner: read a neighbour's value before setting one.** In ddflow a LOWER priority number runs sooner: read a neighbour's value before setting one. On 2026-10-17 I filed and 'raised' a dozen tasks with 55-85 meaning urgent, which put them behind most of the queue; B-perf-lazy-cli went from 30 to 85. Before setting --priority, `ddflow show` two comparable items and copy their scale; after a bulk change list the result sorted by priority. `[L-priority-lower-runs-sooner]`

## python

- **Run ruff format (and ruff check) on the Python files you touched before every commit.** Before committing or running the item's gates, run 'uv run ruff format <touched files>' and 'uv run ruff check <touched files>'; put pure formatting changes in their own commit. Agents must not leave formatting to the pre-push hook or to CI. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-format-python-before-commit]`

## queue

- **A task that needs a decide task is stuck for good once the decide task is abandoned as a decision.** Do not put a decide task in another task's needs; the decision record governs by globs. If one is there, drop the edge with ddflow update --needs once the decision is recorded. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-needs-on-decide-tasks]`

## regions

- **A new pre-commit check must be run against the repo's own generated files.** Before enforcing a digest/marker check on staged files, run it over this repo's real README and docs _(first paragraph)_ `[L0882c63568]`
- **Three ddflow:begin marker grammars coexist.** A check over ddflow:begin/end markers must know all three: doc/name sha= (regions.py), legacy doc=X body-sha256=, and adopt's NAME ddflow=V fmt=N sha= (pins/adopt) _(first paragraph)_ `[L53e89e74bc]`

## registry

- **A declared command needs three registrations by convention: declared file, parser by_convention, lifecycle re-export + wire_shape.** A new declared family needs help_group, wire_shape, no top-level api import in declared/, and its api function re-exported in api/lifecycle/__init__ _(first paragraph)_ `[Lf4b2138e22]`

## research

- **Read vendor docs as raw sources: summarising fetches hid Copilot's cost model change and Antigravity's wrapping ban.** For per-agent facts use curl on raw markdown/HTML (github/docs, vscode-docs, product docs) and grep the text; check the billing page's date before trusting a cost lever _(first paragraph)_ `[Lfe27a174cb]`

## review

- **Making advice runnable makes it dangerous: when a remedy stops naming a nonexistent command, re-check every condition under which it is printed.** A remedy string that names a command which does not exist is inert: whoever follows it gets an error. Correcting it to a real command (git worktree remove, ddflow cleanup --apply, a delete) activates every place it was ever printed, including cases the old text was wrong for. Before turning advice into a working destructive command, enumerate the states that reach it (adopted/harness-owned trees, … _(first paragraph)_ `[L-fix-activates-advice]`
- **A reviewer's finding is not evidence until it is reproduced; refute it against the probe before acting.** On B-docsync-mutants the only cross-family reviewer (Qwen, config-disabled for off-contract output) first returned no counterexample, then on a later pass returned two findings that inverted its own first pass (claiming two tests pass on their mutant); the per-mutant runs showed both were false. A reviewer's output is a hypothesis: reproduce it before it changes anything, and record the refutation when it does not hold. `[L-reviewer-findings-need-repro]`
- **a socket read timeout is not a wall-clock bound.** a stated time bound on a network request needs a timer that closes the socket; the read timeout restarts with every byte a loaded server sends _(first paragraph)_ `[L-socket-timeout-not-wall-clock]`
- **When the operator changes a decision mid-task, rewrite the item's body the same moment.** A cross-family review judges the diff against the item's title and body as its intent. If a decision changes after the item was filed (here: minor bump -> patch bump), update the body when the change is made, or every review reports the correct code as contradicting the spec -- four findings and a failed critic gate for a change that was right. _(first paragraph)_ `[L01d0ae4af6]`
- **A capped manifest must say what it dropped.** Any list in a reviewer prompt that is capped (names, files) ends with 'and N more'; the manifest's own 4-name cap hid for_review and the reviewer called it missing _(first paragraph)_ `[L06190c3d27]`
- **When reviewers flip a design choice back and forth, write the contract down and pin every case with a test.** On a choice with two defensible answers (which side of a synthetic merge to keep, which fallback to take), state the contract in the docstring and README, add one test per case of the contract, and triage the next flip against the contract instead of flipping the code _(first paragraph)_ `[L37bd16e05b]`
- **The roborev daemon leaks a .kilo process per review, which saturates the shared LAN reviewer.** Before and during long review work, reap orphaned '.kilo run' processes (ppid 1); run one review at a time per LAN endpoint _(first paragraph)_ `[L7214df6377]`
- **With the refute-not-review reviewer, a round always finds something: batch fixes and stop editing the diff between rounds.** Collect all findings from one concurrent rubber_duck+critic round, fix or refute them together, then re-run both once; do not commit between a round's start and its result. _(first paragraph)_ `[L90e9fd2e27]`
- **An unreviewed review chunk is not a full pass: re-run it before recording the gate passed.** A review gate with an unreviewed chunk is partial, not passed: re-run that chunk with --chunk N first. `[La16d7f8291]`
- **A delta review sees one commit, so a fix landed earlier on the branch reads as 'no fix'.** After a follow-up commit on a fix branch, expect the deepseek delta reviewer to report 'the diff does not fix the bug' / 'the test cannot fail'; refute with the earlier commit and its failing-first probe, or run --full so the reviewer sees the whole branch. _(first paragraph)_ `[La3224a6276]`
- **A review finding that a new file is empty is the chunker, not the diff.** When ddflow review reports a newly added file as empty or hunk-less, check the file exists with content and treat the finding as the split_diff header-only-chunk artefact (bug B-split-diff-header-chunk) until that is fixed. _(first paragraph)_ `[Lb031f0d60c]`
- **A reasoning-model reviewer at low temperature loops until its token budget is gone.** Run reasoning-model reviewers at the vendor's recommended temperature (DeepSeek: 1.0), not ddflow's 0.3 default; before blaming chunk size or reasoning_effort, read the reasoning tail _(first paragraph)_ `[Lf3feebf5d3]`
- **Reviewer outage mid-loop: unavailable delta overwrites a passed round.** when the LAN DeepSeek is down, do not start a delta round after a passed one _(first paragraph)_ `[Lf6504cb6ca]`

## roadmap

- **Every task adds its exemptions to the same line of constants-exemptions.toml, so merges conflict.** Append new exempt entries at the END of the [exempt] table, never at its top _(first paragraph)_ `[L5705894ec1]`

## roadmap-review

- **Check the queue before applying review-proposed edges; operator answers can contradict each other.** Before applying a roadmap-review edit list, re-read each task's current needs/globs: five edge fixes were already in the queue, and two same-day accepted decisions (D-config-layer-order vs D-jinja-trust-reaffirmed) disagree on where jinja_extensions lives. _(first paragraph)_ `[L7bf40895d6]`

## roborev

- **roborev: a repo .roborev.toml overrides [REDACTED:path]; check a FRESH job's recorded model after changing either.** After changing roborev model/agent, enqueue a fresh review and read its model field in 'roborev list --json'; queued jobs keep the model and prompt they were enqueued with. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-roborev-repo-config-overrides]`
- **ddflow copies .roborev.toml into each worktree at creation: changing the primary's reviewer pin leaves older worktrees on the old model.** After changing .roborev.toml (model, backup) or a served model name, update the copies in existing worktrees (.ddflow/worktrees/*/.roborev.toml), then check a fresh job's model in 'roborev list --json'. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-roborev-worktree-copies-stale]`

## shardmarks

- **a sticky 'lost events' flag set by one look at a shard mid-rewrite.** when a detector's flag is sticky, a single unlocked read of a file another process rewrites in place must be re-looked until it stops changing before it flags _(first paragraph)_ `[L-shrunk-flag-mid-rewrite]`

## shell

- **Never put backticked commands in an unquoted bash heredoc: they execute.** Write files containing backticks with the Write tool or a quoted heredoc ('EOF') _(first paragraph)_ `[L5b24c38a3f]`
- **pgrep -f inside a wait loop matches the loop's own command line and never ends.** Wait on a file or a pid, never on pgrep -f of a string the waiting command itself contains _(first paragraph)_ `[Lc8195d4e78]`

## snapshots

- **Never run 'pytest --snapshot-update' under xdist: parallel workers corrupt the .ambr file.** Regenerate syrupy snapshots with -n 0 _(first paragraph)_ `[Lefd9e3bc02]`

## split

- **A task split with `ddflow split` closes when its children are done: do not try to complete the parent.** A task split with `ddflow split` closes when its children are done: do not try to complete the parent. fleet-trunk3 stopped on a refused `ddflow complete SE-kind-data` that was already done. After the last child completes, `ddflow show PARENT` instead of completing it. `[L-split-parent-closes-itself]`

## testing

- **Mutation-test a file from a saved copy, never undo the mutant with git checkout while the file has uncommitted edits.** Before mutating a file to prove a test fails, commit the real edit or cp the file aside; restore with cp from that copy _(first paragraph)_ `[L-mutate-from-backup]`
- **A baseline test run must use a tree nobody is editing.** Baseline in a detached worktree of the base, never in the tree being edited. `[L6c104fb7d1]`

## tests

- **A test double that counts a request in flight until AFTER it writes the response measures the socket, not the work.** Release a request counter when the work it represents ends, BEFORE writing the response; assert concurrency by that mechanism (the count during the work), never by a wall-clock ratio. A counter kept until after wfile.write/response-send is descheduled under load, so a strictly sequential client reads its count as 2. _(first paragraph)_ `[L-fake-inflight-is-work-not-socket]`
- **Before creating a test module, check the path AND the basename are unused.** Check path and basename before adding a test module. `[L-new-test-file-check]`
- **When tests fail after a deliberate behaviour change, bisect to the commit and update the TEST; fixing the code reverts the change.** When tests fail after a deliberate behaviour change, bisect to the commit and update the TEST; fixing the code reverts the change. Reading the commit that changed behaviour (git log -S) told the agents which side was wrong in minutes. git log -S on the asserted text, read the commit message and decision, then change the test with the reason. `[L-test-vs-code-after-behaviour-change]`
- **A pinned transcript must not hold what varies by Python version or by machine.** Normalise argparse layout (usage wrapping, choice quoting) on both sides of a pin through tests/pin_norm.stable, and fix OS user, host name and PATH tools in the harness; never record them from the developer's box. _(first paragraph)_ `[Lb931674ab8]`

## workers

- **Machine-local gates.toml pins -n 24, so the {workers} default never reaches the unit_tests gate here; /tmp/claude-1001 shared names clash between agents.** Put {workers} in .ddflow/local/gates.toml to use the computed count; write scratch output under the session scratchpad, never /tmp/claude-1001/<name> _(first paragraph)_ `[Lf36d1826eb]`
